newsitem.title: UK: British oil output picks up but no surge in sight.
newsitem.headline: British oil output picks up but no surge in sight.

text.p: British oil production is starting to recover from the technical problems and new field delays which dogged the sector for much of 1996 but it is too soon to forecast a surge in output, industry sources said on Friday.

Early production from Amerada Hess' Fergus and Telford fields -- the latter came on stream in late October over two months ahead of schedule -- and the addition of more new fields before the end of 1996 should boost fourth quarter output.
October also saw Italy's Agip bring on its Thelma field two months early. Thelma should eventually reach peak output of some 50,000 barrels per day (bpd), feeding into the Forties system.

But leading North Sea consultants Wood MacKenzie said they saw little reason to raise their mid-year forecast of an additional 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the October-December period due to new start-ups.
"I think there's enough scope not to raise those figures," said WoodMac analyst Stephen Scullion.
In September, WoodMac forecast U.K. oil output would average some 2.6 million bpd this year, only 20,000 bpd up on 1995's average.
Scullion said he saw little reason to change the yearly figure either, despite improved performances from BHP's Douglas field in Liverpool Bay and British Petroleum's Harding.

Over optimistic expectations for some of the more mature fields, the possibility that severe winter weather will reduce offshore loadings and further delay new fields were factors which could bring the final tally down, industry sources said.
Britain produced 2.5 million bpd of oil in September, up 167,000 bpd from August as seasonal maintenance work drew to a close, The Royal Bank of Scotland said on Friday.
Three more fields, with peak capacity of about 120,000 bpd, should come on stream on the U.K. Continental Shelf before the end of the year.
Of the three, Texaco's Captain field in the central North Sea is by far the largest.
It should start pumping in early December and will eventually reach a peak of some 65,000 barrels per day to be exported via tankers.
Amoco's 7,000 bpd Arkwright, which will feed the Forties system, may slip into early December, industry sources said.
Flotta system throughput should rise as Conoco's 50,000 bpd MacCulloch field starts up in December.
"The new fields coming on before the end of this year will impact more towards the end of the first quarter (1997)," Scullion said.
The most significant increase in production in early 1997 should come from BP's Foinaven field, the first to be developed in Atlantic waters west of the Shetland Islands.
It was originally due to start pumping in June this year but was delayed by a strike at the shipyard building the floating production vessel and a faulty subsea manifold.
"It may be mid-year once Foinaven kicks in before we see a jump in output," Scullion added.
